title: Chapter 79
content:
"Are you genuinely all right? He didn't... torture you, did he?"

If you count being impaled on a massive cock as torture, then sure.

Jakyeong offered nothing more than a sullen shake of his head. Over a late lunch on the villa's patio, the three operatives had begun dissecting the botched getaway. Thankfully, while Jakyeong had been held in captivity on the southern island, Il-hyun had left the brothers completely unharmed.

Ryun let out a low whistle, shaking his head at the memory. "Dropping out of a chopper with a sniper rifle and rolling fragmentation grenades onto the roof... I have to hand it to him. President Kang has serious balls."

Han sighed heavily into his coffee. "Which is precisely why I told you running off was a death wish."

"Next time, tackle me," Ryun shot back. "Beat the shit out of me if you have to."

Jakyeong scoffed around his cigarette. "Giving up after one little bump? What's there to be terrified of?"

Ryun shivered theatrically. "Easy for you to say! When that helicopter banked around and opened up, I thought the devil himself had descended from the sky. I nearly pissed my pants on the spot. Go ahead, feel my trousers—they're probably still damp."

Jakyeong’s shoulders slumped, a dark, self-deprecating mutter escaping his lips:

"Don't flatter yourself. I actually did pee."

He ground his cigarette butt into the flagstones and pushed himself up. Ryun blinked, asking what he had just mumbled, but Jakyeong kept his mouth shut tight. Admitting that he had been fucked so relentlessly he squirted like that was a secret he would take to his grave.

As he exhaled a long, weary breath toward the clouds, the heavy iron gates rolled open.

Two estate security guards marched up the drive carrying a massive, person-sized wooden crate that looked suspiciously like a bespoke coffin.

Han and Ryun got to their feet. What the hell is that?

A terrible intuition struck Jakyeong. The silicone clone. He had prayed the monstrosity had been incinerated during the crash, but following the guards inside confirmed his worst fears. They dropped the crate in the foyer, prying the lid back to reveal the full-scale anatomical replica lying peacefully on a bed of packing foam.

Han and Ryun’s jaws dropped.

"Wei... is that... you?"

"No."

"Don't give me that. It's your spitting image."

"It's a vague resemblance at best. It's not me."

Denials were useless. While the brothers marvelled over the lifelike sculpting, Kang Il-hyun emerged from his study, smoothly instructing the staff to haul the crate up to Jakyeong’s second-floor suite. Having been caught red-handed breaching his contract, Jakyeong lacked the leverage to protest, forced to watch the creepy effigy get hauled up the stairs.

Ryun followed it up, cheekily tugging at the mannequin's waistband before grimacing in shock. "Holy shit. It's anatomically complete."

Han leaned in, equally curious. Poking the material, he was surprised to find the synthetic flesh soft and pliable rather than rigid plastic. The brothers promptly dragged Jakyeong over, standing him side-by-side with the mold for a direct comparison. While they didn't strip Jakyeong’s pants to measure, the consensus was clear: the real thing was significantly more blessed.

"If you're going to commission custom art, you might as well be generous," Ryun mused. "Why make his dick so modest?"

"Right?" Han agreed. "A man has his pride. President Kang was petty for that."

"Wei, you must be pretty insulted, huh?"

"Both of you, shut the fuck up," Jakyeong hissed.

The heavy bedroom door swung open, and the temperature in the room plummeted to absolute zero.

Kang Il-hyun stood on the threshold. Han and Ryun immediately tensed, glancing toward the exit, but Il-hyun stepped inside and clicked the door shut behind him, his dark gaze sweeping over the three operatives.

Ryun forced a loud, hearty laugh, gesturing to the mannequin. "Exquisite taste, President Kang! Truly an inspired housewarming gift."

Il-hyun offered a radiant, razor-thin smile. "Indeed. I was originally planning to have him taxidermied on that island after he ran, but I simply couldn't bring myself to end his life."

"Ah... so it wasn't just a gift... it was a substitute for a corpse..." Ryun swallowed hard, his smile turning brittle.

A dangerous, predatory glint flared behind Il-hyun’s irises. "If you'd like, I can have bespoke replicas cast for the two of you as well."

Both brothers waved their hands in frantic, synchronized refusal. The message was loud and clear: Break your leash again, and you'll be mounted in glass. The silicone figure suddenly looked infinitely more terrifying.

"I imagine you have plenty to catch up on after a few days apart, so I will take my leave," Il-hyun said smoothly. "Chief Park will brief you on your next operational target tomorrow morning. Get some rest until then."

With a polite, elegant nod, he stepped into the hall and pulled the door shut.

The trio exchanged wide-eyed looks, letting out a collective, shuddering sigh.

"We picked the wrong mark to cross, didn't we?"

"Taking the advance and running was a catastrophic miscalculation."

"To celebrate our miraculous survival... should we open a bottle of scotch?"

"Count me out," Jakyeong muttered. "I'm going to bed."

Shaking off Ryun’s persistence, Jakyeong retreated into his private quarters. Between the chronic sleep deprivation and the deep, throbbing aches running through every joint, he felt like he’d been run over by an armored truck. Hearing the outer living room fall quiet, his brothers had clearly retreated to their adjoining suite.

Standing before the vanity mirror, he peeled away the medicated patches plastered across his neck and shoulders. He had burned through more pain-relief supplies enduring Il-hyun's bedroom appetites than he ever had taking shrapnel in the field. Beneath the adhesive, clusters of dark purple bruises bloomed across his skin. Lifting his shirt, his ribs and stomach were covered in identical love bites and friction marks.

Collapsing face-down onto the mattress, a phone chimed on the nightstand.

It was the flagship handset Il-hyun had gifted him—the one he’d abandoned in the getaway car.

Glancing at the caller ID, Jakyeong’s eye twitched.

My Darling ♥

When the hell did he edit the contact name?

He let it ring, but the persistence was relentless. Cursing under his breath, he swiped accept.

[Asleep?]

"Lying down..."

[I have to attend a family dinner at the main estate tonight. I might be late.]

"..."

[May I come up and see your face before I leave?]

The man had developed an infuriating habit of asking for permission, acting like a polite gentleman everywhere except in bed. The faint fingerprint bruises still encircling Jakyeong's throat served as a glaring testament to what the man had done just hours ago.

"I'm sleeping. I'm exhausted."

Cutting the connection, Jakyeong sprawled out like a corpse. Staring at the ceiling moldings, he took in the quiet comfort of the suite. Disturbingly, the place was beginning to feel familiar. Will I ever actually be able to walk away from this cage?

Sleep refused to come, chased away by a tangled knot of unresolved thoughts.
The atmosphere in the grand dining room of the Kang family estate was as frigid and suffocating as a high-society wake.

A lavish multi-course feast stretched across the long banquet table, yet dining under this roof always felt to Il-hyun like attending his own Last Supper. With cold corporate calculations spinning behind his eyes, he traded smooth, superficial pleasantries about subsidiary earnings and logistics.

"Did you enjoy your little holiday?" Chairman Kang asked, cutting through his prime rib.

Il-hyun offered a respectful nod. "Yes, Father."

"Did you travel alone?"

Il-hyun let out a quiet scoff. Why bother fishing when your hounds have already sniffed out every detail?

"Yu-jung dropped by the villa late last night."

Having taken extended leave, his sister was lingering at the coastal resort through tomorrow, sparing her from tonight's family gathering. Though the rest of the table appeared engrossed in their meals, Il-hyun could feel every ear straining to catch the nuance in his tone.

"She hid in the dark trying to surprise me," Il-hyun added, his voice carrying the light, conversational cadence of an amusing anecdote. "I mistook her for an intruder and drove the car straight through the front porch."

"A mistake?"

"I assumed someone had sent a crew to take my head."

Il-hyun smiled warmly, as if sharing a charming joke. Across the table, Kim Sun-young froze for a fraction of a second, her wine glass hovering mid-air. Chairman Kang, however, remained entirely unbattered, chewing with stoic indifference.

Kang Tae-han, seated opposite, scowled in open disgust.

"How do you survive living like that? The sheer paranoia would have put me in an early grave."

Il-hyun’s smile thinned into a razor's edge. "I manage just fine, brother. After all... I'm not you."

The subtle, venomous slight hit its mark, but Tae-han held his tongue to keep the peace, glaring daggers into his linen napkin.

Noticing the predatory tension, Seok-joo seized the lull, timidly clearing his throat:

"I... ran into Jang Yi-an recently."

He deliberately omitted the part about the high-end narcotics club.

Il-hyun didn't flinch, continuing to slice his meat without a flicker of emotion.

Tae-han swirled his vintage Bordeaux, glancing over. "Jang Myung’s grandson? The one with those filthy, bedroom eyes?"

The steak knife in Il-hyun’s hand paused for a single, imperceptible beat.

He shifted his gaze toward his older brother, who continued casually:

"He was lodging at your place last year, wasn't he? What brings him back to Seoul? Did you spot him at some underground venue?"

Seok-joo gave a hesitant nod.

Tae-han clicked his tongue in bemused contempt. "And here I thought he was some sheltered, delicate little heir. Guess art students really are degenerates under the surface. Still, turning up without contacting the family is odd. Did you hear anything about this, Father?"

"Silence," Chairman Kang barked, cutting the conversation dead. "Eat your food."

Tae-han clamped his jaw shut.

Chairman Kang resumed eating, his piercing gaze drilling into Il-hyun. Il-hyun remained the picture of absolute composure—calm, serene, and entirely detached, like a man listening to a stranger's gossip.

Yet how long that polished veneer would hold was a volatile gamble.

Cruising along the expressway back to his estate, Il-hyun cracked the window, lighting a cigarette against the rushing night air.

He felt utterly drained—the family dinner had been more exhausting than a full-scale tactical skirmish. He loosened the knot of his silk tie, undoing the top buttons of his collar. Exhaling a thick ribbon of smoke into the slipstream, he stared out at the passing streetlights.

Resting on the leather seat beside him was the birthday gift Chairman Kang had presented earlier.

Il-hyun pulled the velvet box open, revealing a flawless, pale jade ceramic drinking cup. He let out a low, dark chuckle, running his tongue along the inside of his teeth. In the rearview mirror, he caught Park Tae-soo’s wary glance.

A gyeyeongbae.

In his prime, Chairman Kang had made a habit of sending this exact artifact to business rivals and syndicate lieutenants right before purging them. It was an unsubtle, lethal warning: Know your place. Overreach, and you will bleed for it.

So it finally comes to me.

Il-hyun tossed the porcelain back into its velvet recess, thrusting the box toward the front passenger seat.

"Tae-soo."

"Yes, President Kang."

Il-hyun took a slow drag from his cigarette, a wicked, demonic grin pulling at the corner of his lips.

"Hold onto this. We'll set it out on the old man's memorial altar when the time comes. Let's see who ends up drinking from it first."

Translator’s Note:

  • Gyeyeongbae (계영배): Literally translates to "cup that warns against fullness" or "cup of full caution." It is a traditional Korean cup engineered with an internal siphon siphon mechanism: if liquid is poured up to 70% of its capacity, it holds normally; if poured beyond that threshold, the entire contents drain out through the bottom. Historically, it was used by ancient scholars and rulers as an allegorical reminder against unchecked human greed, overreaching ambition, and excessive indulgence. In the context of Chairman Kang, gifting it serves as a lethal underworld warning that the recipient is reaching too far and will lose everything if they don't know their place.
